articleBody:
Before signing an agreement or purchasing materials for a lower-level renovation, walking through a detailed inspection checklist prevents surprise expenses and schedule delays. Use this checklist to review your space before hiring a contractor.

- [ ] Measure egress window openings — Emergency escape windows in planned bedrooms must meet local clear opening height, width, and sill-height dimensions.
- [ ] Inspect concrete walls for dampness — Trapping water behind fresh drywall leads to hidden mold and structural issues down the line.
- [ ] Verify ceiling clearance around ducts — Main duct trunks and plumbing pipes can lower finished ceiling heights below standard living space requirements.
- [ ] Locate the main water shutoff and electrical panel — Wall layouts must preserve clear, safe physical access to critical home utility equipment.
- [ ] Check existing rough-in plumbing locations — Adding a bathroom is significantly simpler if below-grade drain lines and vent stacks are already stubbed into the concrete.
- [ ] Confirm furnace and water heater clearance — Fuel-burning mechanical appliances require adequate combustion air and maintenance clearance specified by safety codes.
- [ ] Draft a scaled floor plan — Municipal permit offices require drawings showing exact room dimensions, window locations, and utility boundaries.
- [ ] Review contractor licensing and trade coverage — Ensure your contractor coordinates qualified trades for specialized electrical and plumbing rough-in tasks.

How to use this checklist
Review these items during your initial walk-through so you understand what structural or mechanical adjustments your layout demands. When you are ready to evaluate layout options and trade requirements, reach out to HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
